summary: Indigenous scholars made visible after the 1.201 split. Eleven Indigenous scholars whose rows had moved to, or were drafted only in, community-engaged research or ethnohistory gain rows in Indigenous-authored history & critique, so the People Circles place them there: McCallum, Wheeler, Macdougall, Innes, Leddy, Sidney, Kitty Smith, Ned, Shawn Wilson, Witgen and Blackhawk (fields are not exclusive). The nine person entries of 1.201 open with each scholar's sourced, self-stated nation; Witgen's and Blackhawk's identity notes gain their sourced statements.
authorization: User, 2026-10-28: 'Mary Jane Logan McCallum is a member of the Munsee Delaware Nation'; 'the people circle doesn't have her in the Indigenous-authored history group'; 'same with Wheeler'.
rationale: Revision 1.201 moved community-engaged strands and their roster rows out of indigenous, and the coordinator removed self-stated nations from person descriptions on the assumption that identity notes are displayed; they are not on the person profile. Rows are added only where a sourced statement of nation or community exists (identity notes and the 1.201 evidence files: Columbia CSER and Yale profiles for Witgen and Blackhawk). Held for a sourced statement: Rita and Jackie Huggins, McHalsie, Mamani Condori; Rivera Cusicanqui is not classified. OCAP review of 2026-10-27 applies: nation only, no ancestry or family detail.
